Subject: Initial: BYO-KMS requirements and onboarding questions

Hi Olga —

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is a concise requirements doc from our security team (noblehealth_byo_requirements.pdf). High-level asks:
- Hardware-backed key custody inside our VPC (we require HSM attestation / FIPS 140-2 level 3 or higher).
- Support for customer-owned root KEKs (BYOK) and the ability to import wrapped keys during cutover.
- Clear audit trail: per-key creation/import events, operator actions, and key rotation history retained 7+ years.
- Operator separation: we need to be able to define an escrow / split-operator model.
- Network model options: VPC peering, PrivateLink, or on-prem SRvC; we need port and CIDR requirements to scope firewall changes.

Can you share Redwood's suggested minimum network firewall rules, HSM models you support, and a proposed rotation/escrow pattern we can review? Procurement looped in CC for timeline visibility. We hope to have an onboarding window in late Sep.

Cheers,
Alex Carter
Director, Infrastructure Security
NobleHealth

Alex —

Thanks for the clear requirements doc and the timeline. Quick responses inline and an initial plan below.

Inline:
- HSM models & attestation: Redwood supports FIPS-capable HSMs (Yubico/Thales/Entrust family in our Dedicated/private options). We can accept either hardware-attested device certificates or perform a remote attestation flow depending on your preference.
- BYOK import: we support importing wrapped KEKs (PKCS#12 or KMIP-wrapped blobs) during cutover; we also support sealed-key flow where private key material never leaves your environment.
- Audit & retention: we can stream key events to your SIEM (syslog/OTLP) and maintain a separate immutable audit export for up to 7 years if required (add-on).
- Operator separation: recommend split custody for root KEK + operator workflow we outline below.

Proposed next steps (hand-off checklist):
1) Network discovery: Alex provides VPC CIDRs, peering option preference, and a test jump host IP by Sep 17.
2) HSM attestation POC: Redwood to run a small attestation test (Jonas owner).
3) Import/runbook: Redwood to share a configuration template + minimal ACLs (attached: redwood_private_byo_checklist_v1.pdf).
4) Operator runbook & access matrix: Tessa will draft operator separation matrices and rotation cadence suggestions.

A few clarifying Qs:
- Do you require dedicated physical HSM appliances on-prem, or will a VPC-attached HSM in our private deployment suffice?
- Any restrictions on outbound telemetry from the HSM subnet?

If that plan looks good I propose a 30-minute sync early next week to lock cutover dates.

Best,

Subject: Re: Initial: BYO-KMS requirements and onboarding questions

Alex / Olga / team —

Adding ops-level detail and recommended defaults from our side so you can share with your infra/security teams.

Operator & rotation recommendations:
- Root KEK: recommend customer-controlled root KEK with split custody. Two-person approval for any key import/unwrap operations.
- KEK rotation cadence: 12–24 months for KEK (depending on risk profile). Data-encryption keys (DEKs) rotated more frequently (90 days).
- Emergency eviction & zeroize: operator role separation enforced via RBAC + a cryptographic zeroize protocol (documented in runbook).
- Backup & escrow: recommend encrypted escrow key stored offsite (split shards) with notarized access procedures.

Network & connectivity (minimal rules to start):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to Redwood control-plane endpoints for attestation and metrics.
- Open TCP 8732 (KMIP) or 5696 (vendor-specific) only if using KMIP; otherwise, prefer HTTPS-wrapped import APIs.
- Peering: VPC peering or PrivateLink both supported — PrivateLink reduces exposure and avoids cross-account route table changes.

I've attached a starter access matrix (kms-access-matrix.xlsx) and a link to our operator runbook template. I will draft the detailed operator separation matrix and a sample canary cutover checklist by Sep 18.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kms-access-matrix.xlsx
From: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@noblehealth.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.example.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: BYO-KMS requirements and onboarding questions

Alex / team —

Quick technical clarifications from the HSM/attestation side:
- Attestation flow options: (A) HSM supplies hardware certificate chain which we verify during onboarding; (B) remote attestation TLS-style handshake where the device proves firmware/hardware state to our verifier. Option A shortens cutover.
- Ports & connectivity for attestation & telemetry: TCP 443 (control), UDP 514 or TCP 6514 for syslog (if you push logs to our collector), and ephemeral ranges for RPC depending on vendor — we'll provide a vendor-specific port list once you confirm a model.
- Key import formats: PKCS#12 wrapped with password+HSM-wrapped token OR KMIP Transfer syntaxes. We support an import verification step that generates an import proof event in the audit log.
- SIEM & traceability: we can emit structured JSON events to your SIEM endpoint; recommend a dedicated ingestion endpoint with TLS client auth.

I've attached a lightweight attestation flow diagram (hsm-attestation-flow.svg) — this illustrates the short path (cert check + on-demand challenge). From a rollout perspective I recommend one staging host + one production host, initially in separate subnets, and a canary traffic split for 48–72 hours.

I'll take the owner for the attestation POC; can we schedule the POC week starting Sep 21 (test window)?

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Security & Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
